https://www.theyeshivaworld.com/news/isr.text: UMAN CHAOS: Thousands Fear Rosh Hashanah Flights Could Be Canceled As Airlines Await Israeli Approva August 27, 2026 6:35 pm 4 Comments Thousands of Breslover travelers planning to spend Rosh Hashanah in Uman are facing growing uncertainty, with numerous charter flights still lacking the necessary takeoff and landing slots from Israel’s Airports Authority — and foreign airlines warning that flights could be canceled entirely. According to a report by B’Chadrei Chareidim, the first travelers are expected to begin their journeys as early as Sunday, but many charter flights already sold to passengers have still not received final slot approvals from Ben Gurion Airport. The greatest pressure is expected between September 7 and 10 for departures from Israel, and September 14 through 16 for return flights. Among the airlines reportedly still awaiting approvals are Electra, Cyprus, SkyUp, Albastar, HiSky and FlyOne. Foreign carriers have reportedly warned that they cannot indefinitely hold aircraft and crews without confirmed operating times and may ultimately be forced to cancel flights if approvals do not arrive soon. The situation has triggered anger among travelers who say the massive annual Rosh Hashanah pilgrimage to Uman is known years in advance and should not repeatedly descend into a last-minute logistical crisis. “It’s simply Chelm, there’s no other word,” one Yerushalayim resident who purchased tickets for himself and his two sons told B’Chadrei Chareidim. “The trip has existed for almost 40 years. The dates are fixed on the calendar. This coming Sunday people are already starting to fly, and there are still no approvals!” He recalled previous years in which travelers were forced to sleep on the terminal floor with young children because of slot-related delays. Another traveler from Beit Shemesh said families have already spent thousands of dollars preparing for the trip. “We paid thousands of dollars. You can’t play with people like this,” he said. “We feel there is no one in the country taking responsibility for us.” Numerous travelers have now appealed to Rav Natan Ben Nun, chairman of Ichud Breslov in Uman, asking the organization to urgently intervene with the Israel Airports Authority before the situation becomes irreversible. Complicating matters further is the ongoing war in Ukraine, which means travelers cannot fly directly into the country and instead must land in neighboring countries, particularly Romania, before continuing overland to Uman. Romanian and Ukrainian authorities require detailed transportation plans in advance so they can prepare border crossings, security personnel, buses and other infrastructure for the enormous influx of travelers. Without final flight slots from Ben Gurion Airport, those schedules cannot be completed — raising fears that delays in Israel could create a cascading logistical crisis stretching from the airport through Romania and into Ukraine. Officials involved in organizing the annual pilgrimage warned that unless the slot issue is resolved within the next day or two, large numbers of travelers could potentially find themselves unable to reach Uman for Rosh Hashanah, while suffering substantial financial losses on flights, accommodations and food already purchased. “This is an event that is known in advance,” one official involved in the travel arrangements said. “You can’t operate by putting out fires every year when the flights are about to leave.” The official called on the Airports Authority to begin treating the annual Uman travel operation as a permanent, predictable national event rather than an unexpected crisis each year. ( YWN World Headquarters – NYC ) 4 Responses The annual pilgrimage to Uman for Rosh Hashanah is a fixed point, known well in advance. Yet, each year, the logistics seem to unravel at the last minute, leaving thousands of travelers in limbo. This pattern of predictable chaos, where the known becomes a crisis, suggests a failure to see the event for what it is: a recurring, deeply significant movement of people. The true challenge lies not in reacting to an emergency, but in recognizing the enduring nature of the journey itself. All these flight tickets were sold subject to regulatory approval. There is a war going on in the Middle East. If the flights are cancelled, those who paid will be entitled to have their ticket payments refunded. Everyone who has booked in the past few months knows what the score is. If going to Uman is so important, then happily take any financial risks involved without complaining. If it is, don’t buy tickets and reserve accommodation, etc. etc. The only ones who will suffer if they are not able to use their tickets are those who are taken to a Military Prison when they try to leave the country illegally.
